method: One glyph chain over the whole line, fitted on the paragraph lines of the public practice training pages only (3,306 lines without uncertain readings). Each line is one string of symbols: its glyphs, a word-space symbol between words, a line-end symbol after the last word. The only fitted statistic is how often each symbol follows the four symbols before it. A line is written symbol by symbol, starting afresh at each line, until the line-end symbol is drawn. No word list, no copying, no rule naming a glyph. The first glyph of a word depends on the last glyph of the word before it only through the chain's context, and that context is emptied at each new line, so the dependence is present inside lines and absent across line breaks by construction of the procedure, not by a rule about the statistic. A line holding a four-word run of the manuscript is redrawn (seed 408, 3,000 lines). On the practice split, with whole lines kept, the within-line minus across-break gap is 0.151 bits against 0.173 for the manuscript (threshold 0.08, above the within-page shuffle). A chain that runs straight through line breaks keeps its dependence across them and shows no gap (P-L2-001). So the fact needs a writer who treats the line as a unit, not language.
